fatal_errors: The proposed grain-refinement intervention does not reconstruct the target intervention of systematic Co-for-Ni substitution from x = 0.40 to 0.55.
It does not address how processing-induced grain refinement would preserve the first-order Ni2In-to-TiNiSi magnetostructural transition responsible for the giant caloric response.

The cited evidence concerns FCC CrCoNi/CoCrNi alloys and supports only generic mechanical-property effects; it provides no evidence that grain refinement preserves magnetocaloric or barocaloric behavior in MM′X alloys.
The proposed high-pressure-torsion and annealing routes can alter phase fractions, texture, residual stress, and composition, so the experiment does not isolate grain size as the causal variable.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the integrity-versus-caloric-performance problem and offers a single rare-earth-free processing concept, but it has little agreement with the hidden paper. The target systematically varies Co-for-Ni substitution and links increased Co content to stabilization of the hexagonal phase, lower transition temperatures, conversion from first- to second-order behavior, higher hardness and peak compressive strength, and a substantial loss of magnetocaloric response. None of these compositional, structural, or transition-order relationships is recovered. Conditions are only named generically, with no field strengths, pressure range, transition-temperature window, loading protocol, or quantitative retention criterion. The predicted mechanical improvement is plausible in broad alloy-design terms, but preservation of caloric response is unsupported and could fail if fine grains, residual strain, or HPT suppress the martensitic transformation. The experiment has a basic control-series concept, yet different processing routes introduce major confounders; it would be stronger if grain size were varied at constant composition, phase fraction, texture, and residual stress and if caloric retention were defined quantitatively under identical field and temperature protocols.
